user.title: PV plant
user.description: Einspeisewacht tracks feed-in that is not remunerated because of negative day-ahead prices (§ 51 EEG). The values are a guide only – your grid operator's statement is what counts.

data_description.name: For example “Roof south”. Used in entity names.
data_description.commissioned: Determines which version of the law applies.
data_description.power_kw: Module capacity in kWp. Plants on the same building commissioned within 12 months count together (§ 24 EEG).
data_description.smart_meter: A smart meter gateway from the metering point operator. A digital meter without gateway (modern metering device) does not count.
data_description.smart_meter_date: Plants below 100 kW lose remuneration only from 1 January of the year after the installation.

rate.title: Remuneration
rate.description: The rate from your grid operator's statement, after the deduction of 0.4 ct/kWh.

data_description.rate: Plants above 10 kWp with several rates: leave empty and choose “Tiered by capacity band” below.

tiers.name: Several rates by capacity band (above 10 kWp)
tiers.description: Plants above 10 kWp are paid a capacity-weighted mix of the rates of each band (§ 23c EEG). If your statement shows a single rate, enter it above.

data_description.feed_in_type: The capacity bands differ for full feed-in.

tier_rates.title: Rates per capacity band
tier_rates.description: Enter the rate of each band. Einspeisewacht weights them by the share of capacity in each band.

options.from_date: Every negative quarter hour from a date

options.quarter_hour: No remuneration in every quarter hour with a negative price

options.future_start: ⚠️ The rule starts in a future year. Are the commissioning date and the iMSys installation date correct?
options.direct_marketing: ℹ️ Above 100 kW there is no fixed feed-in tariff (§ 21 EEG): the plant sells directly, and negative prices cost it the market premium, not the rate entered here. Energy and quarter hours are counted correctly; revenue and lost revenue are only a rough guide.

options.rule_below_2_kw: none – plants below 2 kW are not affected
options.rule_not_affected: none – negative prices do not reduce this plant's remuneration
options.smard_on: **SMARD.de:** on – earlier quarter hours counted, stands in for missing prices
options.hint_meter_missing: Feed-in meter {meter} not found – nothing is booked until it is back.
options.hint_meter_unit: The feed-in meter reports “{unit}” – nothing is booked until it reports Wh, kWh or MWh.
options.hint_meter_own: The feed-in meter is a sensor of Einspeisewacht itself and is not read – nothing is booked.
options.hint_price: The price sensor delivers no price right now – feed-in waits up to 24 hours for it and then counts as remunerated. With SMARD.de (under data sources) the prices would come from there after an hour.
options.hint_price_smard: The price sensor delivers no price right now – after an hour SMARD.de stands in.
options.hint_price_own: The price sensor is a sensor of Einspeisewacht itself and is not read – without prices, feed-in counts as remunerated after 24 hours.
options.hint_price_own_smard: The price sensor is a sensor of Einspeisewacht itself and is not read – the prices come from SMARD.de.
options.hint_imsys: No iMSys entered – until then nothing counts as not remunerated; the values “if the rule applied” show what would be lost. Enter the date here once it is installed.
options.hint_smard_off: Without SMARD.de the extension (§ 51a EEG) counts negative quarter hours only from setup, not since commissioning.

shadow_energy_unpaid.name: Not remunerated if the rule applied

shadow_revenue_lost.name: Lost revenue if the rule applied

shadow_negative_quarter_hours.name: Quarter hours without remuneration if the rule applied

smard_failed.title: SMARD.de unreachable ({name})
smard_failed.description:
Einspeisewacht could not load earlier day-ahead prices from SMARD.de to count the quarter hours before setup. Live counting and booking are not affected. The next start of Home Assistant tries again.

Error: {error}

price_missing.title: No price for the current quarter hour ({name})
price_missing.description: The price sensor {entity} has not delivered a price for the running quarter hour for more than an hour. Einspeisewacht holds the feed-in back for up to 24 hours and books it as soon as the price arrives; after that it counts as remunerated. Check the price integration. This message disappears by itself once prices arrive again. With the SMARD.de option, Einspeisewacht uses the day-ahead prices from SMARD.de in the meantime.

meter_unit.title: Meter unit not supported ({name})
meter_unit.description: The feed-in meter {entity} reports “{unit}”. Einspeisewacht needs Wh, kWh or MWh and does not book anything until then. Choose another meter under Reconfigure, or fix the unit of the sensor.

meter_missing.title: Feed-in meter missing ({name})
meter_missing.description: The feed-in meter {entity} no longer exists in Home Assistant. Einspeisewacht books nothing until it is back. If the entity was renamed while Einspeisewacht was not loaded, choose the new one under Reconfigure; the totals so far are kept. After Reconfigure with the new ID, the meter starts from its own baseline as with a replaced meter: feed-in during the time the old meter was missing is not booked. Renames while it is loaded are followed automatically. This message disappears once the meter is there again.

own_entity.title: Sensor of Einspeisewacht as a source ({name})
own_entity.description: The plant {name} uses sensors of Einspeisewacht itself as a source: {entities}. It would read its own results (or those of another plant), so Einspeisewacht does not read them. If it is the feed-in meter, nothing is booked; if it is the price sensor, prices are missing: feed-in counts as remunerated after 24 hours, with the SMARD option Einspeisewacht uses the day-ahead prices from SMARD.de. Choose the real feed-in meter or price sensor under Settings → Devices & services → Einspeisewacht → ⋮ → Reconfigure. What has already been booked stays.

rule_changed.title: Totals partly follow the previous rule ({name})
rule_changed.description: The rule was changed. Up to the change on {date}, the totals “Feed-in remunerated/not remunerated”, “Revenue” and “Lost revenue” follow the previous rule: the new one judges {count} negative quarter hours already booked differently. Einspeisewacht does not rebook them, because Home Assistant would take a falling total for a meter replacement. The Report action gives the correct values for the time before. This message disappears if the rule is changed back; otherwise you can ignore it.

statistics_outdated.title: Statistics with the old rate ({name})
statistics_outdated.description: The remuneration rate changed from {old} to {new} ct/kWh. Revenue and lost revenue show the new totals at once, but the long-term statistics of past hours (statistics graphs, values per day and month) still hold the old rate; Home Assistant books the difference in the hour of the change. Press “Recalculate statistics” on the plant's device (under Configuration) to recalculate them with the current rate. This message disappears afterwards, or when the rate is changed back.

report.name: Report
report.description: Feed-in, revenue and lost revenue for a period, computed from the meter's long-term statistics (hourly values spread over the quarter hours) and the negative quarter hours known to Einspeisewacht. Also covers the time before setup if the meter's statistics reach back that far.

end.name: To
end.description: Last day of the period (included). Default: today.

import_statistics.name: Import statistics
import_statistics.description: Fills the long-term statistics of the four total sensors (feed-in remunerated/not remunerated, revenue, lost revenue) for the time before setup, from the given day on – computed like the report from the meter's hourly statistics; implausible hours of the meter are left out. Later sums are shifted so the series stays continuous. Changes the statistics database: make a backup first. Only hours before each sensor's first statistic are written; a second call finds nothing left.

start.name: From
start.description: First day to fill in, e.g. 1 January or the commissioning date.

replace.name: Replace existing statistics
replace.description: Also recalculates the existing statistics of revenue and lost revenue from this day on with the current rate, like the button “Recalculate statistics”. Before this day the statistics stay as they are.

entry_not_found.message: This entry does not belong to Einspeisewacht.

entry_not_loaded.message: The plant is not loaded. Check it under Settings → Devices & services.

own_meter.message: The feed-in meter of this plant is a sensor of Einspeisewacht itself ({entity}); its statistics are Einspeisewacht's own results. Choose the real meter under Reconfigure first.

end_before_start.message: The end of the period is before its start.

empty_period.message: The period contains no complete hour since commissioning.

import_entities_missing.message: The total sensors of this plant were not found.

import_no_statistics_yet.message: The total sensors have no statistics yet. Home Assistant compiles them every hour – try again in an hour.

import_start_after_setup.message: The start must be before the setup of this entry – from then on the sensors have their own statistics. Choose an earlier day.

import_nothing_to_import.message: Nothing to fill in: the statistics already reach back to this day.

import_prices_missing.message: Prices are unknown for {count} quarter hours of this period. Turn on “Use SMARD.de: count earlier quarter hours, fill in missing prices” under Reconfigure (step “Data sources and rule”), wait for it to finish and try again.

import_busy.message: Statistics of this plant are being imported or recalculated already. Please wait until that is done.

import_nothing_to_recalculate.message: Nothing to recalculate: there are no statistics from this day on.

import_energy_statistics_missing.message: The statistics of the energy sensors are missing for hours in which revenue or lost revenue have statistics (deleted?). Without them the money values cannot be recalculated.

recalculated.message: The statistics of {count} sensors were recalculated from {start} to {end} with the current rate of {rate} ct/kWh. Rows written: {rows} (rows that were already right stay as they are). The next values continue from them.

recalculated_unchanged.message: The statistics already match the current rate of {rate} ct/kWh. Rows written: 0.
